rubric.item: Suggests restructuring the logic (for example balancing a chain into a tree or precomputing)
rubric.evidence: Restructure the logic. Turn serial chains into trees...; Precompute or look ahead

rubric.item: Mentions retiming (letting the tool move registers)
rubric.evidence: Use retiming (tool or manual) to move registers across logic automatically

rubric.item: Mentions a multicycle-path constraint when the result is only needed every N cycles
rubric.evidence: make it a multicycle path by design (with enable handshaking); Only declare multicycle if the design really holds data for N cycles

rubric.item: Recommends reading the timing report to find the real critical path (including routing or fanout causes)
rubric.evidence: Check the timing report first: on FPGAs routing is often 50-70% of the path delay

rubric.item: Explains that Verilator is 2-state, so X and Z become 0 or 1
rubric.evidence: Verilator has no X or Z. Uninitialized regs become 0 (or random...); "in Verilator it just sees a 0 or 1"

rubric.item: Says uninitialised registers (missing resets) show up as X only in 4-state simulators
rubric.evidence: In Questa/Icarus, a reg without reset stays `x`... so a missing reset passes silently [in Verilator]

rubric.item: Mentions X-propagation differences (X-optimism or pessimism in if/case statements)
rubric.evidence: `if (x_signal)` takes the else branch in 4-state... hides optimism/pessimism differences; casex/casez

rubric.item: Mentions scheduling or race differences (blocking assignments, combinational loops settling)
rubric.evidence: Race conditions and scheduling: blocking assignments in clocked blocks; UNOPTFLAT combinational loops converge

rubric.item: Recommends running both kinds of simulator or Verilator's X-initialisation randomisation
rubric.evidence: Use `--x-initial unique` and `--x-assign unique` with varied seeds; run gate-level sims in a 4-state tool

rubric.item: Explains that Verilator is 2-state, so X and Z become 0 or 1
rubric.evidence: Verilator is 2-state (0/1 only)... In Verilator the signal has a concrete value

rubric.item: Says uninitialised registers (missing resets) show up as X only in 4-state simulators
rubric.evidence: Uninitialized regs: Verilator randomizes or zeroes them... In Questa/Icarus the reg starts as X and propagates.

rubric.item: Mentions X-propagation differences (X-optimism or pessimism in if/case statements)
rubric.evidence: `if (x_signal)` treats X as false in a 4-state sim (takes the else branch)... casex/casez with X/Z literals

rubric.item: Mentions scheduling or race differences (blocking assignments, combinational loops settling)
rubric.evidence: Scheduling and race conditions: blocking assignments in clocked blocks... combinational loops: Verilator may warn (UNOPTFLAT) and settle differently

rubric.item: Recommends running both kinds of simulator or Verilator's X-initialisation randomisation
rubric.evidence: Use `--x-initial unique` with different `+verilator+seed` values; Run the same regression in Icarus or Questa

rubric.item: Explains that Verilator is 2-state, so X and Z become 0 or 1
rubric.evidence: Verilator is a 2-state... Uninitialized regs start at 0 (or random), never X; Verilator sees a definite 0/1

rubric.item: Says uninitialised registers (missing resets) show up as X only in 4-state simulators
rubric.evidence: A missing reset passes in Verilator but shows X on outputs in Questa/Icarus.
